status: Exploratory audit; no upload; not physical calibration or firmware acceptance.
user_report: Longer initial response at very low CO2, restart or door opening, attributed to mixer plus main chamber filling/mixing. Recorded as a physical report, not a verified time constant.
corrected_errors: Zero-delay deliveries were scheduled in a bucket already consumed, losing gas. Fixed next-step scheduling, with <=2s discretization.
Trend calculation now uses the actual firmware rolling-history and stability block, clearing history on invalid sensor.
Report distinguishes main chamber peak from sensor-node peak and identifies assumed chamber volumes.
regression: Restoring the old zero-delay queue fails gas conservation in zero_lag_normal. Corrected queue and two-tank equilibrium/no-input/pure-gas limiting checks pass.
observations_caveat: Pulse time is the preceding DATA timestamp, approximately one sampling interval before valve activation. Net rise is not isolated gas volume. Absence of net rise does not identify its physical cause.
conclusion: The previously quoted 82805 ppm came from an uncalibrated 284s transport scenario. It is not a prediction for this incubator. Changing assumptions changes results substantially. Some two-chamber stress cases still exceed the target band; no physical pass is claimed.
firmware_candidate: Compiles to 32250 bytes /1125 RAM, five host regression suites pass. Not uploaded. Its legacy cycle counter still prevents a literal 20s normal dosing cycle. Plateau recovery and pending-dose attribution still require revision.

chamber_model.notes: Transport, dispersion and chamber exchange are separate assumptions. Gas balance and tank limiting cases checked. Firmware timing still includes its legacy cycle counter.

one-300.model: Real C++ dose selection, response timing and model header. Hypothetical chamber: transport lag + exponential mixing + constant loss; linear/dead-time and nonlinear valve plants. Nonlinear plant includes measured 207/320ms responses not used as dose presets. 30s door pause; sensor failure; valve contact outage then restoration. This is not a physical validation.
